messages.body_plain:
Not sure if it is the same issue i ran into couple of days ago. I also updated all packages and the axis labels of my ggplot plots disappeared. Since i did not change my code, i tried to figure out if some packages i automatically load may be incompatible.

In my case, after i removal of ggtern all plots are fine. When i load ggtern, the axis are missing or messed up.

BW, H

On Tuesday, 31 March 2020 22:32:10 UTC+2, Brandon Hurr wrote:

> Using your code I can verify the behavior that you show with a compressed y-axis.
>
> I wonder if it's just something your doing with your scales.
>
> I seem to get a reasonable plot with the following:
> ggplot(ExampleTable, aes(x=Column, y=Row, fill = Number_of_Objects)) + geom_tile() + theme_classic() +
> scale_x_discrete(limits=c(1:24)) +
> scale_y_discrete(limits=c(16:1), labels=LETTERS[1:16])
>
> Here I'm reversing the scale with the limits rather than using -Row in the aesthetics.
>
> HTH,
> B
>

> On Tue, Mar 31, 2020 at 12:49 PM Dahea Diana You <dhy...@gmail.com> wrote:

> > I recently reinstalled my R/Rstudio due to the issue with one of the packages, and during this process, I also (1) downloaded and installed R development tools and libraries (clang and gfortran) from https://cran.r-project.org/bin/macosx/tools/ (2) downloaded and installed gfortran compiler for R from https://github.com/fxcoudert/gfortran-for-macOS/releases/tag/6.3 (3) uninstalled Java/JDK 14 and installing Java/JDK 11 version; and (4) ran “R CMD javareconf” comman on the terminal. All of these actions were taken to resolve the error associated with one of the packages requiring Java connection.
> >
> >
> > However, during theses resolution steps, something else seemed to be messed up because the existing function/package/script started working inappropriately. So the problem is (and this problem is SEPARATE from the package problem that I was trying to solve with the resolution steps mentioned above): I run this script that utilizes several packages including ggplot2, tibble, dplyr, etc. to generate my graphs. Just several days ago when I tried to generate these graphs, the script worked fine (see below picture, on the left labeled as a "good example").
> >
> >
> >
> >
> > But after all the resolution steps that I took as discussed above, the exact same script no longer works properly (see above picture, on the right side labeled as a "bad example" that I'm getting now). I used the exact same script, same packages to generate these graphs but now the graphs are being generated strangely…It seems like the tickmarks on the y axis are now not getting evenly spaced out throughout the whole y-axis and the problem starts at the stage where I create "Plot." Does anyone have any idea what might have gone wrong during the resolution that could have damaged R (or its associated packages) to cause this problem? I want to go back to the ggplot2 that used to create that "good example"
> >
> >
> > The data that I used are basically table of different cell numbers in each well ("Number_of_Objects) in 384-well plate and I tried to depict the data using the heatmap approach as shown in the figure. The figure shows the collection of small rectangles corresponding to each well in 384-well plate and they are colored on gray gradient based on the cell density (darker, the greater density). The code that I used to plot this is:
> >
> >
> > library("tidyverse") library("stringr") library("ggplot2") library("ggpubr") #Table corresponds to the data table of 384-well plate that will be analyzed# Plot=ggplot(Table, aes(x=Column, y=-Row)) + theme_classic()+ scale_x_discrete(limits=c(1:24), name="") + scale_y_discrete(limits=c(-1:-16), labels=LETTERS[1:16], name="") pShape=Plot + ggtitle("Number of non-border cells") + geom_tile(aes(fill=Number_of_Objects)) + scale_fill_gradient(low = "black", high = "gray80", name="")
> >
> >
> > I used the exactly the same script both times and both times the script runs without any error but generates completely different graphs. How can I fix the issue so that I can go back to the "good example" graph state?
> >
> >
> > During install/reinstall, some of those packages used in the script might have been updated as well. I checked the updates on all the packages that were installed and except for "tibble," which is a package that gets called along with those libraries when I load "tidyverse," everything was up-to-date. install.packages("ellipse")

groups_Mb <- interaction(Classifier$Species)

for(g in levels(A$esp_clas)){

                  (as.data.frame(with(A[A$esp_clas==g,],

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

A more minimal example is

library(ggplot2)

exd <- data.frame(x = 1L:4L, y = 1L:4L)

ggplot(exd, aes(x, -y)) +
    scale_y_discrete(limits=c(-1:-4))

I think the issue here is that the y-axis variable is a number but we use scale_y_discrete. That combination is incompatible and there is no reason to expect that it will work.

You can either convert you y-axis variable to a discrete data type, or use a numeric scale:

ggplot(exd, aes(x, as.character(-y))) +
    scale_y_discrete(limits=as.character(c(-1:-4)))

or use numeric values:

ggplot(exd, aes(x, -y)) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits=c(-1, -4), trans = "reverse")

Best,
Ista

You could use code like this:

library(tidyverse)
f.norm.vec<-function(x) {
  x<-x/f.norm(x)
  x
}
f.norm<-function(x) { sqrt(sum(x^2)) }
f.gen.sphere<-function(n=100,p=5) {
  x<-matrix(rnorm(n*p),ncol=p)
  xnew<-t(apply(x,1,f.norm.vec))
  xnew
}
f.vc.ellipse <- function(vc, xm, n=500) {
  p<-ncol(vc)
  x<-f.gen.sphere(n,p)

  evc<-eigen(vc)
  vc2<-(evc$vectors)%*%diag(sqrt(evc$values))%*%t(evc$vectors)
  x<-x%*%vc2

  x + matrix(rep(xm, each=n),ncol=p)
}
